_comment: Seed catalog of external resources Rāma can research for master — free and premium AI/AGI infrastructure. This is a STARTING list, not exhaustive: resourceResearchEngine.cjs re-verifies every entry's live docs on request rather than trusting these numbers to stay current. 'wiredAs' points at the registry key that already exists in code, if any, so the UI can show enabled vs researched-only vs unknown without re-deriving it. Prices/limits last checked 2026-08-13 — see RAMA_AGI_MASTER_SPEC.md Section 38 for sourcing.

resources.name: OpenAI API
resources.notes: No free API tier. GPT-5.6 family; mini/nano variants sub-$1/1M tokens.

resources.name: Anthropic Claude API
resources.notes: Free consumer chat tier exists but the API itself has no free tier. Sonnet 5 ~$3/$15 per 1M tok in/out.

resources.name: Google Gemini API
resources.notes: Free tier ~5-15 RPM depending on model, 5000 free requests/mo shared across 3.x models.

resources.name: Groq API
resources.notes: No card required, full model catalog, rate-limited (~30 RPM). Paid from $0.05/1M tok.

resources.name: Mistral API
resources.notes: Already wired; verify current free trial credit at research time.

resources.name: Ollama (local)
resources.notes: Fully free, offline, no key. The level-0 fallback the whole router leans on under resource pressure.

resources.name: OpenRouter
resources.notes: NOT YET WIRED. ~14 rotating :free model IDs (Llama, Nemotron, Hy3, etc.), single key, no card. Good first candidate for a resource-enable proposal — one integration adds many free fallback models.

resources.name: Local Whisper (whisper.cpp)
resources.notes: Already the L2 target of the voice capability ladder (Section 30). No new integration needed.

resources.name: ElevenLabs TTS
resources.notes: NOT WIRED. Free tier ~10k credits/mo. Premium ~$0.05-0.10/1k chars — most expensive mainstream TTS (~$100-200/1M chars vs OpenAI/Google ~$10-15/1M). Different axis than STT ladder — this is speech OUTPUT quality, not input.

resources.name: OpenAI TTS
resources.notes: NOT WIRED. Cheaper premium TTS alternative to ElevenLabs if voice-cloning quality isn't required. Reuses the same OPENAI_API_KEY already in the vault if set.

resources.name: DuckDuckGo Instant Answer API
resources.notes: Already integrated, unlimited, no key. Correct level-0 fallback for this axis — keep regardless of what else is added.

resources.name: Tavily Search API
resources.notes: NOT WIRED. 1,000 free credits/mo, no card; also has a fully keyless basic tier. Purpose-built for LLM/agent consumption (structured, RAG-ready) — real upgrade over browserEngine's DOM-scrape fallback.

resources.name: Exa Search API
resources.notes: NOT WIRED. ~20,000 free requests/mo — larger free allowance than Tavily. Compare against Tavily in the research report before proposing either.

resources.name: Qdrant (self-hosted)
resources.notes: NOT WIRED. Self-hosted is free, open-source (Apache-2.0), no vector-count cap beyond hardware. Matches the project's 'local before cloud' doctrine — natural upgrade over vectorMemory.cjs's in-memory/keyword fallback with no premium key required.

resources.name: Pinecone
resources.notes: NOT WIRED. Free tier exists but reportedly tightened in 2026. Closed-source, no self-host option — conflicts with I11 (every engine needs a working fallback) unless paired with a local option anyway, which makes Qdrant the more consistent first choice.

design.label: Interface & Design System
design._axisNote: Different in kind from the API axes above: these are assets and libraries, not endpoints, so `credKey` is null throughout and `license` — not price — is the field that decides whether master can use it. Every entry here is free AND redistributable in a shipped desktop app; anything merely 'free to view' is excluded, because bundling it would be a licence breach dressed up as a saving. Licences are seed data like every price above and are re-verified at research time. Nothing here is applied without a ledger proposal master approves (I6), and anything that becomes an npm dependency must be pinned exact (I12).

resources.name: Fluid type scale (CSS clamp, Utopia method)
resources.license: no dependency — generated CSS is your own
resources.notes: NOT WIRED. Highest-value entry for the defect master actually reported: type that is physically tiny on a large panel and wide dead margins. A clamp()-based scale makes font size a function of viewport, so the interface adapts in CSS instead of relying on the zoom fit in appearanceState.cjs. The two are complementary — zoom scales everything uniformly, a fluid scale changes the ratios. Blocked on one real obstacle worth stating: the UI is built from hundreds of inline px fontSize values that no CSS scale can reach, so this needs those values tokenised first, which is a large mechanical change and exactly why it should be a reviewed proposal rather than a quiet edit.

resources.name: Lucide icons
resources.notes: NOT WIRED. The interface currently draws its icons from unicode glyphs (⬢ ◈ ▣ ↕ ↺ 🧹), which render differently on every machine and font fallback — a real cross-platform inconsistency, not a matter of taste. Lucide has a React package, tree-shakes to only what is imported, and ISC permits redistribution in a packaged app. Alternatives on the same licence class: Phosphor (MIT), Tabler (MIT), Remix Icon (Apache-2.0).

resources.name: Radix Colors
resources.notes: NOT WIRED. Dark-mode scales built for verified contrast, where each step has a defined purpose (background, border, text). Would keep Rāma's cyberpunk palette while giving the muted/dim greys an accessibility floor — the low-contrast greys are the reason the System page's own 'Loading disk info...' text was easy to miss. Worth pairing with a stated WCAG target so contrast becomes measurable rather than judged by eye.

resources.name: Open Color
resources.notes: NOT WIRED. Smaller, simpler alternative to Radix Colors — a flat palette rather than a semantic scale. Lower effort to adopt, less help with contrast guarantees. Listed so the research report can compare the two rather than presenting one as the only option.

resources.name: Inter (UI typeface)
resources.notes: NOT WIRED. Designed for screen UI at small sizes, with tabular figures that stop metric readouts jittering as digits change — directly relevant to the CPU/RAM pills and process tables. Would sit alongside JetBrains Mono rather than replacing it: mono for code and data, Inter for prose and labels. OFL 1.1 permits bundling the font files in the installer.

resources.name: Orbitron / Rajdhani (HUD display faces)
resources.notes: NOT WIRED. Squared, technical display faces that suit the existing HUD aesthetic for headings and section labels only — both are poor choices for body text and would hurt legibility if used broadly. Included because it matches the established design language, not because the interface needs another font; a proposal should argue for headings-only scope or drop it.

resources.name: Modern CSS reset + density scale
resources.notes: NOT WIRED. Addresses the second half of master's complaint — the dead vertical space — by replacing ad-hoc inline padding/margin with a spacing scale. Cheap to adopt incrementally, page by page, and unlike the type-scale entry it does not require tokenising every inline font size first. Probably the lowest-risk starting point of this axis.
